summary: Discusses how International Standard Book Numbers can be supported within the URN framework and the syntax from RFC 2141. It is historic. It was replaced by RFC 8254.

eli5.summary: It turns the number on a book's back cover into a permanent online name.

questions: what is the nid for isbn
subtitle: How the number on the back of a book can be used as a Uniform Resource Name.

tldr.problem: Books already have ISBNs, but the URN framework needed a registered namespace and a resolution story before an ISBN could serve as an Internet name.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC embeds the ISBN in the URN syntax as urn:isbn, explains how the group and publisher parts of the number can steer resolution to national bibliographies, and registers the NID ISBN.
tldr.outcome: This memo is Historic and was obsoleted by RFC 8254.

facts.label: ISBN length
facts.value: Ten digits, last may be X

today: RFC 3187 is Historic and has been obsoleted by RFC 8254, which replaces it for the ISBN namespace.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
The IETF URN working group wanted to show that the URN syntax could accommodate identifiers from established namespaces. The bibliographic community was one such source. RFC 2288 had studied ISBN, ISSN and SICI as URNs, and this document analyses ISBNs in more detail. It includes the registration request for the Namespace Identifier (NID) ISBN.

The memo was written by the Helsinki University Library and the International ISBN Agency. Its scope is identification and resolution. ISBNs mostly identify finite, manageable objects, and a book may exist only in print. In that case the best a resolver can offer is bibliographic data from a national bibliography, including where the physical copy is held.
sections.eli5: Books have numbers, and this note asks whether those numbers can be turned into names that work online.

sections.title: ISBN Structure and URN Syntax
sections.content:
An ISBN identifies an edition of a monographic work and is defined by NISO/ANSI/ISO 2108:1992. It is a ten-digit number, and the last digit can be X. It has four variable-length parts, usually separated by hyphens: a group identifier for a group of publishers, a publisher identifier, a title identifier, and a modulus 11 check digit that uses X instead of 10.

Every character of an ISBN is valid in a URN, so percent-encoding is never needed. The example is URN:ISBN:0-395-36341-1. Before comparing two ISBN URNs, hyphens are removed and any letter x is converted to uppercase. The memo also notes plans to extend the ISBN to 13 digits by putting the 978 or 979 EAN flag in front.
sections.eli5: The book number has parts, like a street address: a region, a publisher, a title, and a last character to check for typos.

sections.title: Resolving ISBN URNs
sections.content:
The structure of the ISBN helps resolution. The group identifier hints which national bibliography to ask. For example, group 951 means Finland, so the Finnish national bibliographic database can resolve the URN into bibliographic data or, if the resource is online, the document itself.

Some groups cover a language area. Group 3 is used in Germany, Austria and German-speaking parts of Switzerland. There are two answers: define a cascade of resolution services in the DNS records, or define the publisher identifier ranges assigned by the International ISBN Agency in the DNS. The second is better because the correct service is found immediately.

The group identifier is sometimes misleading, notably in the US and UK where international companies publish. A large union catalogue such as WorldCat could be a fall back. A publisher could also run its own service, and requests for its prefix, such as 951-0, would go to that server.
sections.eli5: The first digits of a book number say which country's library to ask. If that guess is wrong, a giant shared catalogue is the backup.

sections.title: Assigning ISBNs and Handling Mistakes
sections.content:
The delivery format does not matter: if the content qualifies, it gets an ISBN. Each format of a digital publication should have a separate ISBN. A new edition is normally based on a change in packaging (hard cover, paperback, library binding, or different digital file formats) or a change in the text beyond minor corrections. The RFC admits that interpretation is somewhat subjective and varies by publisher, and an ISBN URN will often resolve to many URLs.

Publishers occasionally re-use an ISBN, which the memo treats as a rare human error. In the resolver it typically returns two or more bibliographic records, and the user picks the right one. National bibliographies and Books in Print correct mistakes and add cross references from the incorrect ISBN to the correct one.
sections.eli5: Each version of a book gets its own number. If two books share one by mistake, the lookup shows both and you choose.

sections.title: The Namespace Registration
sections.content:
The registration is for NID ISBN, version 1, dated 2001-01-25, registered by Hartmut Walravens of the International ISBN Agency. The RFC explains that giving the NID ISBN to any other identifier system would cause confusion.

ISBNs are assigned by group agencies, often in national libraries, and publishers receive blocks of numbers. The International ISBN Agency approves group agencies, allocates group identifiers and publishes the group and publisher prefixes. The registration says an assigned ISBN should never be re-used and that it stays with the publication, so it is persistent. Validity can be checked with the modulus 11 check digit, and assignments can be checked with group agencies or publishers. Scope is global.
sections.eli5: This is the official sign-up form that claims the name ISBN for book numbers and explains who hands them out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo encodes ISBNs in the URN framework and describes resolution only generically, so secure or authenticated resolution is excluded. It does not deal with validating the integrity or source of URNs that contain ISBNs. Intellectual property rights for identified objects, and rights to the databases behind resolvers, are also out of scope.
sections.eli5: The note does not try to prove who made a name or lock anything down. It leaves that for other work.

items.title: Check digit
items.text: Modulus 11, with X in place of 10.
